title: Medicare Independence at Home Medical Practice Demonstration Improvement Act of 2015
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it passed the Senate on April 22, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Medicare Independence at Home Medical Practice Demonstration Improvement Act of 2015

(Sec. 2) Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to increase from a three-year to a five-year period the length of an agreement with an independence at home medical practice under the Medicare Independence at Home Medical Practice Demonstration Program.

summary.headline: This law lengthens the agreement period for Medicare home-based medical practices in the Independence at Home demonstration from three years to five years.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Medicare Independence at Home Medical Practice Demonstration Program. Before this law, a participating practice signed an agreement that lasted three years. Under this law, the agreement lasts five years. The summary does not describe other changes to the program.

who_it_affects.group: Medical practices that take part in the Independence at Home demonstration program
who_it_affects.how: Their agreements with Medicare now run for five years instead of three.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare beneficiaries who receive care through these participating practices
who_it_affects.how: Their practice's program agreement can now last longer, but the summary does not say how this changes their care or coverage.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate effective date. The law was enacted on July 30, 2015.
